# Torque budget — DAST-1, 2026-11-18

*Generated by [mechlint](https://github.com/amirhpd/mechlint) `torque` from
`src/description/urdf/description.urdf.xacro` and `mechlint.yaml`. Regenerate with the command
at the bottom rather than editing the numbers here.*

## The question

Does the drive train in `mechlint.yaml` hold each joint of the 6-DOF arm, empty and with
100 g / 200 g at the tip?

## The answer

**Yes, every joint passes at 200 g — but the wrist only just.** joint_4 (1.09×), joint_6 (1.11×)
and joint_5 (1.26×) are all close to the limit at 200 g. At 100 g every joint keeps at least
2×. The shoulder and elbow (joints 2–3, DS51150 at 12 V) have plenty of margin.

| Joint | Drive | Supply | Available | empty | 100 g | 200 g |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joint_1 | DS3240MG | 6 V | 2.360 N·m | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| joint_2 | DS51150-12V | 12 V | 11.040 N·m | 1.421 (3.88×) | 1.945 (2.84×) | 2.471 (2.23×) |
| joint_3 | DS51150-12V | 12 V | 11.040 N·m | 0.570 (9.68×) | 0.970 (5.69×) | 1.370 (4.03×) |
| joint_4 | MG996R | 6 V | 1.100 N·m | 0.038 (14.64×) | 0.272 (2.02×) | 0.507 (1.09×) |
| joint_5 | MG996R | 6 V | 1.100 N·m | 0.026 (21.04×) | 0.232 (2.37×) | 0.438 (1.26×) |
| joint_6 | MG996R | 6 V | 1.100 N·m | 0.032 (17.44×) | 0.265 (2.08×) | 0.498 (1.11×) |

Worst-case |torque| at the joint in N·m over 2048 sampled poses, including every corner of the
joint-limit box, with the margin in brackets. Margin = available / (torque × safety factor 2.0);
a joint passes at margin ≥ 1. joint_1 turns about the vertical axis, so gravity applies no
torque about it at any pose — that zero is real, and it means joint_1 is sized by friction and
acceleration, which mechlint does not model. It still has to start and stop 932 g of arm.

Worst pose for joint_4 at 200 g (rad): `joint_1 +1.361  joint_2 -0.917  joint_3 -0.663
joint_4 -1.528  joint_5 +0.931  joint_6 -1.481`.

Worst pose for joint_2 at 200 g (rad): `joint_1 +0.772  joint_2 -1.460  joint_3 +0.091
joint_4 +1.165  joint_5 -0.471  joint_6 -0.031` — the upper arm tilted almost flat.

## Mass each joint carries

| Joint | Carried (arm only, no payload) |
|---|---|
| joint_1 | 932.2 g |
| joint_2 | 916.3 g |
| joint_3 | 670.5 g |
| joint_4 | 309.8 g |
| joint_5 | 196.4 g |
| joint_6 | 34.1 g |

These include every motor further out on the chain: the joint_3 DS51150 and the joint_4 MG996R
on `link_2`, and both wrist MG996R on `link_4`.

## What these numbers are, and are not

- **Static.** Gravity holding, nothing accelerating. A real move needs more. That is what the
  safety factor is for, and 2.0 is a convention, not physics.
- **Torque sources, all `low` confidence.** DS3240, DS51150 and MG996R are bench measurements
  (stall, lever on a scale), not continuous ratings.
- **Masses are estimates,** from the STLs at PLA 1.24 g/cm³ and 30 % infill, plus each drive's
  mass from the actuator database, placed at the positions in `mechlint.yaml`. Only the Kinect
  (500 g) is weighed.
- **`base_1.stl`, `link_2.stl`, `link_3.stl` and `link_4.stl` are not watertight** (M001), so
  their masses come from a convex hull — an over-estimate. link_3 especially (113.4 g) looks
  high. Every joint from 2 to 5 carries one of these, so those margins are pessimistic by
  whatever the hulls add.
- **The Kinect is not in any of this.** It is eye-to-hand, beside the robot, so no joint carries
  it. mechlint works that out from the chain: every joint between it and the world is fixed.

## Related findings

`mechlint check` also reports **U007** on every joint: each declares `effort="20.0"` N·m, which is
1.81× what the DS51150 delivers, 8.47× the DS3240 and 18.2× the MG996R. A controller clamping
above what the drive can do is not clamping.

## Reproduce

```bash
mechlint torque -P 0 -P 100 -P 200      # the table
mechlint inertia                        # the masses
mechlint check                          # plus units, tensors, masses, meshes
```
